intention: A TREE NODE HOLDS ONE CLAIM, NOT EIGHT. A verdict deposits as its PARTS — one node per verdict and per disposition, each with its own honest vector — and the whole verdict is DERIVED BY READ from the parts, never stored twice. why:
THE CEILING WAS NEVER THE PROBLEM — IT WAS THE MESSENGER. MEASURED 2026-07-29: A's verdict is 11283 chars as one node (1.5x over), while its largest single part is 2097 and its smallest 1267 — every part fits with 3.5x headroom. So the wall is GRANULARITY, not capacity, and the embed host refusing was Law 3 doing its job: it surfaced a node-shape error. Look at what one vector over 11283 chars of eight distinct claims actually IS — a centroid of eight unrelated things, pointing nowhere in particular. Eight vectors each pointing at one claim is MORE ACCURATE, not merely smaller. The monolith was already the wrong shape before it was too big; truncation would have hidden the finding and split the vector from its content, which is why it was refused rather than trimmed.

AND THE CLOSE MECHANISM ITSELF IS CAPPED. Stone C's verdict came in at 6418 of ~7400 — I got it under the ceiling by writing DELIBERATELY TERSE evidence, by hand, at close. That is an operator compensating for a missing physics, and the next stone over is a coin toss. [[solidify-the-layer-below]]: a problem surfaced in a lower layer (the deposit/embed seam) and future builds are already unconsciously compensating for it, which is how a 'proven' whole quietly stops being proven. Every subsequent stone's close rides this seam, so it is not Stone A's private blocker — it is the close mechanism's blocker, and it goes in front of the queue.

provenance: Cast 2026-07-29 through /sorted, at the end of a design arc Akien opened with 'many web servers handle dynamic pages. what would it take to do that here? and if we did, should we also build a separate compositor device?' — the analogy was the whole insight: a dynamic page is COMPOSED AT REQUEST TIME FROM PARTS THE SERVER DOES NOT OWN, which is the shape the tree was missing. THE COMPOSITOR DEVICE WAS DECLINED, on Cairn's own rules and not on preference: two composers with different consumers is premature abstraction (nothing-rides-loose's horizon states the second-proves / third-earns rule), and Law 6 points the other way — every projection in Cairn is owned by the owner of the data it projects (projector for state, pending() for the ledger, render.py for pages), so a compositor device would take composition AWAY from the data's owner and add a hop while owning nothing. A thing that owns no state and produces no data is a FUNCTION, not a device. Seeded by A being back-edged off a falsified PROVED at 6d3ea5b ('the loop fires in anger and finds a ceiling').
